source.title: Adversarial Rademacher Complexity of Deep Neural Networks
source.authors: Jiancong Xiao; Yanbo Fan; Ruoyu Sun; Zhimin Luo

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper. Its front matter identifies a 2026 JMLR publication and an arXiv v2 dated 8 July 2026, while the catalog ID is arXiv:2211.14966.
record.tranche_reason: The paper reports a clean train–test generalization gap for VGG-19 on CIFAR-10, but its experiments focus on adversarial robustness and do not test any listed claim version. The clean-gap results are recorded as findings outside the mapped versions.
record.gate_note: The paper's adversarial-training results and robust generalization gaps concern adversarial examples, which are outside the claim's stated scope. The clean generalization-gap comparison in Table 2 is recorded under fits_no_version. Cited results from other work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study derives adversarial Rademacher complexity bounds and compares standard and adversarial training. Its own results test none of V1–V8: clean generalization gaps alone do not establish those versions, and weight-norm correlations do not measure V7's magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' empirical interpretation, but omits their main theoretical contribution: bounds on adversarial Rademacher complexity for deep networks. The authors attribute poor robust generalization to an adversarial-setting factor and an algorithm-dependent norm-to-margin factor, reporting empirical correlations. They acknowledge that their bounds are numerically vacuous in practical experiments.
record.recipe_differences: Studies adversarial Rademacher complexity bounds and robust generalization on VGG architectures; it does not use the listed studies' interventions or measurements for the mapped claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that weight decay changes robust generalization gaps and weight norms, with training performance declining at larger decay values. These results concern robust generalization.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG-19 on CIFAR-10 has 0% clean training error under both training methods; clean test error is 10.45% after standard training and 26.34% after adversarial training.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For this VGG-19 experiment, adversarial training increases the clean train–test error gap relative to standard training.

record.peer_reviewed: Journal of Machine Learning Research 27 (2026), as stated in the supplied text
record.problems: The recorded clean-gap comparison is for one architecture and dataset; no uncertainty estimates are reported. The paper's central experiments concern robust rather than standard generalization.
record.rows_left_out: No other rows were retained. Adversarially robust gaps and weight-decay results in Section 6 and Appendix C.4 concern adversarial examples and are outside the claim's scope; cited prior-work results were excluded.

untested.parts: No fixed random-label fitting or comparison of natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
No width sweep measuring test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
No convolutional versus fully connected comparison or intervention on local connectivity.
No adaptive optimizer versus SGD comparison or optimizer-tuning comparison.
No batch-size comparison under fixed epoch budgets or adapted recipes.
No dropout intervention or joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation. Weight-decay experiments alone do not test this version.
No magnitude-scaled weight-perturbation tolerance measurement or ranking against norm- and margin-based measures. Norm products and input-adversarial robustness measure different quantities.
No memorization-based example selection, removal, or retraining comparison.

record.verdict_notes: Change the record's relation from tests to discusses; T6 is appropriate. The exclusion rests on the specific interventions and measures required by V1–V8, not on adversarial training being categorically outside generalization research. The robust-gap and weight-decay results are already declared in rows_left_out and require no missing entries.

versions.untested_parts: No random-label fitting or natural-label versus random-label test-accuracy comparison.
No width sweep beyond the interpolation threshold.
No convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparison.
No comparison of adaptive and non-adaptive optimizers.
No dropout comparison; weight-decay findings concern robust generalization gaps.
No magnitude-aware sharpness measurement or comparison with norm- or margin-based measures.
No memorized-example removal or retraining comparison.
